tips.comment: Cameletta Vega started her career with a win in a bumper at this meeting last year and returned to the winner's enclosure last time, switching to hurdles at Cork, making all to comfortably win a mares' maiden hurdle 82 days ago. She made one mistake at Cork, but otherwise, she looked a decent hurdler in the making and could cope with the rise in class.

Won impressively on hurdles debut last time, winning with plenty in hand, hardly having come off the bridle. Pleasing to the eye, looking an exciting hurdling prospect and should have a good chance in this.

The model I run suggests Keep Up can win this one. Keep Up lines up here with the second highest RPR of the smaller 10-horse field but has an official ranking that leaves him looking well treated off this mark. He has shown some form coming into this with figures of 15-1 and needs to show more improvement against stiffer opposition. The jockey on board relieves a further 7 lbs, which helps over the trip. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Won at Downpatrick, then again at Perth. Looks the progressive type. Has good speed and stamina. This race is harder but should be bang there.

Looks stable 2nd string here based on jockey bookings, but has won their maiden/novice hurdles last twice in good fashion and does look to be an improving juvenile hurdler. Good jockey back up and top trainer has done well here last 5 seasons, making current 16/1 decent Ew value in the race.

Not out of it despite the price. Showed ability when runner-up on penultimate start and now returns to similar conditions. Has experience, a rider in form, and looks a sneaky each-way contender at a track that often favours bold early moves. One for the shortlist at huge odds.

Has looked a winner in waiting since being sent handicapping, shaping as if he is desperate for the step up in trip. His pedigree would suggest that the longer distance is going to be a big plus for him.
Has some good recent form and this drop back in trip ought to help. Has won over farther and if stamina becomes a factor, ought to be involved.

Although 0-8, I think Eagles Dream is potentially the sort of horse to pick up a big prize in the future. He finished 4th here on Monday, which was a good run. There has been money on today, so obviously a big run is expected. Definitely one to keep an eye on.
Could be a lively each-way option. Has run over this distance on the flat before and is much better off at the weights this time around. Could go well.

The model I run suggests Garrick Painter can win this one. Garrick Painter lines up here with the second highest RPR of the larger 18 horse field and is the highest rated official ranking. This leaves him carrying the joint highest weight around this 1m 4f round trip. Drawn in stall 6, so shouldn't pose too many problems from a draw perspective over the longer 1m 4f distance. Comes here after a huge time away and hasn't run for over a year, hence the huge price. But if near good form and race fitness is there, could go close. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

A past winner over 1m4f on heavy ground at Bellewstown, who has good form with cut in the going and often runs well, finishing in the frame multiple times, and is capable of a bold show this afternoon.

Spin over jumps was better than the flat, but this race was the plan for a while. Hasn't run since May, but was a good second then, and any rain will enhance her chance. First five places here with some bookies, and no way is she the cooked horse only after 6 runs, and still may be better than the bare form suggests.

Enziya flunked somewhat on his AW debut earlier this month but previous to that the grey won in impressive style when getting up on the line at Limerick. A repeat of that should see him reach the frame.
Went close here last year and now, after a change of stables, can go well again under a new and capable rider from a good draw.
Looks a huge price here and loves the ground. Trip to suit as well and a good jockey on board. Should run a big race.

Not showing the benefits yet for a drop in ratings, Quiz Test is now one pound above his only win that came at Cork. He's been running over longer distances, but this drop back to twelve furlongs may help, and he is competently weighted.

Natalia Lupini (SR 25%; winner here this week) trained handicap debutant Dreamed To Dream is bred for staying trips by Arc winner Sottsass out of (Derby winner) Camelot mare. Steps up in trip now and much less exposed than many. Leigh Roche rides.

Unexposed 4yo, just four career runs. He was a runner-up on his handicap debut two weeks ago and 5L clear of the rest. No chance behind the smart winner, but to be fair to the selection, the winner was an unexposed 3yo who was raised 16lb for the win. The selection runs off the same mark in this handicap and could still have some improvement in him.
They are stepping this up in trip with the same 3 lbs jockey on board. Worth a small each-way saver bet for the 5 places available.
Had this at 8-1 earlier, not that long ago really and is being backed right in. I got this tip from a mate and has joined Gavin Cromwell and looks the one to be on here.

Warttime Leader is a 5-year-old son of Churchill ex Katiyra who won at Group 2 level at 1m2f. Last time out on his racecourse debut in a 4-year-olds only bumper, he finished 1 length second at 9/2 behind Shuttle Diplomacy 100/30f by Dschingis Secret in January '24. That bumper has produced three winners from two runners. He'll now be ridden by Mr. P.W. Mullins for his father W.P. Mullins in this 2m2f bumper. I think he can progress here and break his maiden tag. I make him my Nap of the day.

The model I run suggests Garahon can win this one. Garahon lines up here with the second highest RPR of the 17-runner field but has not been penalized for it in the weights. All horses step out carrying the initial same amount of weight around this 2m 2f national hunt flat. Garahon came an improving second on last outing 26 days ago and can build on from that to get over the line first. Headgear applied for the first time to help - tongue tie added for the first time. Unsure if noteworthy or not - but only horse wearing headgear. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Wide open race and Plumped for this one for the win bet. Proven handicapper and can keep improving to take this race today.

Winning PTP who cost 120,000 sterling for current connections. Will benefit from a fast run race here so will hopefully get that, good Good amateur retains ride and in hands of a shrewd trainer, making current 20/1 decent Ew value in the race.

This is the one i had picked myself at a better price than my win tip.(still dropping in price) This was bought for £85k not long after winning the Oldcastle p to p and has probably come on a lot since then. Small ew.
Small yard in good form and one of the more experienced amateur riders on board. Nice debut effort and the time figure was respectable.

Bold Rhyme is not entirely ruled out. Two fair efforts in bumpers so far, both this month. Has stayed on in each of those (by Yeats out of a Supreme Leader mare, so has that ability). Feasible he could progress further on third start. DM Christie trained.
Let's get a surprise like yesterday at Goodwood, eh? Hoping we can get a place here. Unexposed, and who knows? Stamina needs to be proven, but let's sneak third.
